The pattern of global ROM loss — with internal rotation most affected — is more characteristic of capsular tightness than isolated impingement or tendinopathy, which usually spare internal rotation and show more focal pain on specific provocative tests (not documented, but notably *absent* from exam summary). The chronicity (~2 months) aligns with the “freezing” phase. Although labs are pending, the lack of systemic features (no fatigue, no joint swelling elsewhere, no morning stiffness >30 min, no extra-articular manifestations) makes inflammatory arthropathy unlikely as primary driver.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Insidious-onset left shoulder pain persisting ~2 months without trauma or prior injury  
- Pain aggravated by extreme ranges of motion (overhead reaching, behind-the-back movement)  
- Nocturnal pain disrupting sleep  
- Active forward flexion limited to 75° with pain  
- Active abduction limited to 75° with pain  
- Active external rotation limited to 45° with pain  
- Active internal rotation severely restricted to 15° with *significant* pain — the most pronounced limitation  
- Normal rotator cuff strength on resisted testing  
- No local signs of inflammation (no swelling, erythema, warmth, deformity)  
- No neurologic symptoms (no numbness, tingling, weakness)  
- No cervical spine symptoms (no neck pain/stiffness radiating to shoulder)  
- Plain radiographs (AP, scapular Y, axillary views) all normal  

[GAPS]  
- Passive range of motion values — critical to confirm global capsular restriction (adhesive capsulitis requires *both* active and passive ROM loss)  
- Results of MRI and ultrasound — needed to rule out subtle rotator cuff tear, biceps tendinopathy, or synovitis  
- Laboratory results (ESR, CRP, RF, anti-CCP, HbA1c, TSH, etc.) — to exclude low-grade inflammatory, autoimmune, or metabolic contributors (e.g., diabetes is a major risk factor for adhesive capsulitis, but confirmation pending)  
- Performance and findings of specific physical exam tests (e.g., capsular pattern assessment, coracoid pain test, passive ROM comparison) — not documented  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Adhesive capsulitis
